title: WebBrowserSessionError
description: Closed error body of the WebBrowserSession routes (AF-CTR-05 part C1; Plan decision Q14; ArcForges-Design web.md "Contract gap" and errors.md): the JSON the center sends for a refusal of a /session/v1/web/* JSON route, an ArcError in the WebBrowserSession conventions (UUIDs as lower-case text, instants as RFC 3339 UTC, 64-bit integers as decimal strings). A companion of public/http/v1/web-browser.schema.json, which stays unchanged; it has no route of its own. Shape validity is not authentication of the reply.

WebBrowserErrorReply.title: WebBrowserErrorReply
WebBrowserErrorReply.description: The body of a refusal of a WebBrowserSession JSON route (public/http/v1/web-browser.schema.json, /session/v1/web/*): Content-Type application/json, the reply of the center instead of the route's own response root. error is the ArcError of the refused call (foundation.v1, ArcForges-Design errors.md) in the document's JSON conventions. The HTTP status follows the category: 403 for authentication, authorization and entitlement; 400 for validation, conflict, state and RESOURCE/quota_exceeded (413 for a body over the route's bound and 415 for a media type or content encoding the route does not admit); 404 for STATE/not_found and STATE/not_activated; 429 for RESOURCE/rate_limited; 503 otherwise. A client reads the error member, never a message text. On a hosted center the Worker answers some requests to the same routes itself in text/plain without this body (400, 403, 405, 408, 413, 415 and 429 before the center; 499, 503 and 504 that can follow a call the center has begun or finished, so a 499, a 504 and a 503 without Retry-After never mean that the center did not see the request), and a disabled surface is its 404. The center itself answers an unknown or disabled path (404) and a method other than the route's (405) without a body. Such replies carry no ArcError and are not this document.

WebBrowserArcError.title: WebBrowserArcError
WebBrowserArcError.description: foundation.v1.ArcError as JSON: category, retry mode and effect as the lower camel case of their enum names; code the errors.md code; messageKey error.<category>.<code>; correlationId the call's correlation ID (the one in the center's log); details the single detail of the error, omitted when there is none. Rule webBrowserErrorAdvice: messageKey is error.<category>.<code>; retryAt is present exactly when the mode is afterTime and reconciliationOperation exactly when it is reconcile (the foundation rule retryAdvice); the effect unknown never pairs with afterTime (the rule arcError).

WebBrowserErrorRetry.title: WebBrowserErrorRetry
WebBrowserErrorRetry.description: foundation.v1.RetryAdvice: mode; retryAt the earliest retry (RFC 3339, UTC) of an afterTime advice; reconciliationOperation the fully qualified read method of a reconcile advice.

WebBrowserErrorStateFailure.title: WebBrowserErrorStateFailure
WebBrowserErrorStateFailure.description: foundation.v1.StateFailure: state and reason (both present, errors.md reply rules); resource only with a real 16-byte ID, the ID the caller named or the caller's own object. Never an e-mail address or other personal data.

WebBrowserErrorResource.title: WebBrowserErrorResource
WebBrowserErrorResource.description: foundation.v1.AggregateRef: the object's kind and its ID.

WebBrowserErrorLimitFailure.title: WebBrowserErrorLimitFailure
WebBrowserErrorLimitFailure.description: foundation.v1.LimitFailure as the center sends it: limitName; maximum (a canonical decimal) when the limit has one; recoveryAt (RFC 3339, UTC) when the limit recovers at a known instant. LimitFailure.available is not carried.

WebBrowserErrorRevisionConflict.title: WebBrowserErrorRevisionConflict
WebBrowserErrorRevisionConflict.description: foundation.v1.RevisionConflict: the expected and the actual revision, as decimal strings.
